newsitem.title: USA: Minnesotan proposes flogging drunk drivers.
newsitem.headline: Minnesotan proposes flogging drunk drivers.

text.p: A Minnesota state legislator proposed Tuesday that drunk drivers should be flogged or humiliated in public.

Judges should be empowered to punish habitual drunk drivers with a public whipping or by forcing them to stand on a street corner with a sign saying, "I am a drunk driver," Republican state representative Tom Workman proposed.
"I'm not looking to split the skin on your back, though I think people would want you to feel some pain," Workman told reporters.

His proposal, at present informal, looked unlikely to get far. The chairman of a state legislative committee, Wes Skoglund, called the plan "frivolous and unconstitutional" and a step backward to the Dark Ages.
Commenting on the idea, a spokeswoman for the Minnesota chapter of Mothers against Drunk Driving argued that shaming drunk drivers does not work. She urged more vigorous enforcement of existing laws.
"There are people with six or seven DWI (driving while intoxicated) convictions and who are in public life. They have no fear of humiliation at all," spokeswoman Robin Scholer said.
